content.text:
Yes, as long as you both push to the same GitHub repo. Entire stores what it records inside git and syncs it through `origin`, so Flo gets your history the way they get your commits.

**What gets shared**
- **Checkpoints** (session transcripts linked to commits) are pushed to `origin` as hidden git refs under `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`. Five from your earlier session are already on the remote. Flo's checkpoints go to the same place.
- **The repo config** is committed, so Flo already has it on a normal pull: `.entire/settings.json`, the Claude Code hooks in `.claude/settings.json`, and the Codex hooks in `.codex/hooks.json`.
- **The Entire web app**, once an org admin imports the repo, shows both of your sessions. Access follows the GitHub collaborator list.

**What stays on each machine**
- **Sessions still in progress** stay local until they're committed and pushed. Things like `.entire/metadata/`, `tmp/` and `logs/` are gitignored, so Flo won't see this session until you commit.
- **Login** is per person: Flo signs in with their own GitHub account.
- **Git hooks** live in `.git/hooks`, which git never shares, so Flo has to install them on their machine.

**What Flo needs to do**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
```
```bash
entire login
```
```bash
entire enable
```
Then they work as normal. `entire status` and `entire doctor` will confirm everything is wired up.

One limitation: Entire doesn't sync live between you. You see each other's agent context only after one of you commits and pushes. If you want Flo's agent to build on yours, push often. Entire Brain could also help: it turns the shared sessions into memory that both agents read. I haven't set it up.

I think we see it now and connected, can you quickly give me a table of each feature it provides, with one sentence each and how we can use it https://hack.entire.io/agentic-ai-hack-zurich-2026/#connect

Here's each feature from the hackathon page, with a suggestion for how we could use it in PlanWorldSimulator.

| Feature | What it does | How we can use it |
|---|---|---|
| **Checkpoints** | Links each git commit to the agent session and the decisions behind it. | Commit as usual and say yes to linking. Later, `entire checkpoint explain HEAD` shows why something was built a certain way, such as the world-server decision 0004. |
| **Agentic Search** | Searches past commits, sessions and decisions by meaning or exact text, across pushed repos. | Before starting a feature, run `entire search "world simulator tick loop"` to see what you, Flo or an agent already tried. |
| **Entire Graph** | Gives the agent a map of the code so it can find implementations, follow relationships and check what a change affects. The page claims up to 71% token savings. | Run `entire plugin install graph` and `entire graph init-agents --repo .`. The agent then searches the graph instead of grepping. `entire graph stats` shows how many tokens it saved. |
| **Entire Brain** | A memory layer stored in the repo that every agent reads, so context carries across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. | You and Flo, and different agents, can hand work to each other without re-explaining. Rejected approaches and decisions carry over. It needs Graph installed first. |
| **Agent integrations** | Records sessions from supported agents (Claude Code, Codex and Cursor are enabled here), and the Agent Integration Protocol lets you add others. | Use whichever agent you like and everything ends up in one history. Codex still needs its hooks approved in `/hooks`. |
| **Trails** | Entire's take on code review: each Trail is backed by a GitHub PR, and Runners review every push and post findings. | Request access through the Trails form. Then turn on Runners and Trails in the repo settings, run `entire runner setup -y`, and use `entire trail create` instead of opening a plain PR. |
| **Doctor** | Finds stuck sessions, hooks that no longer match the config, and checkpoint branches that have come unlinked. | When a session or checkpoint doesn't show up, run `entire doctor`. Adding `--force` fixes everything without asking. |
| **Docs MCP** | Makes the Entire docs searchable by the agent through MCP. | Run `claude mcp add --transport http entire-docs https://docs.entire.io/mcp` so I can look up Entire answers myself. |
| **Recap / Dispatch / Activity** | CLI summaries of recent work recorded in checkpoints. | Use `entire recap` or `entire dispatch` for a quick sync between you and Flo, or for the demo. |

The last row comes from the CLI's `--help` output, not from the hackathon page.

For the hackathon, Graph and Brain look most promising for a project idea. "Hand off work between agents" or "Prove what Continuous Memory saves" would fit well with two of you working on the same repo.
